items.title: Gerald Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Snooky Young comes out to join Lee Young, whose brother Lester Young is coming to join his brother on sax, and they’re all going to open up this club in Los Angeles with Billie Holliday.

ctx.x: So did you meet Gil? Did you get to know Gil?

Oh I know Gil, oh yeah I knew Gil real well yeah Gil was – he was with Les Hite’s band. See Dizzy and – and Gil Fuller played with Les Hite’s band. So when – when Les Hite came back to California, Dizzy and Gil Fuller didn’t come back, but they had a whole book full of Gil’s arrangements, and that’s when I went and joined Les Hite’s band. Now, you’re gonna want to hear this now. This is about Snooky Young, he’s back on the scene now. Look here. Snooky Young comes out to join Lee Young, whose brother Lester Young…
number like it was nothing, you know what I mean? And Benny was – he was so happy with that band. He was just really happy with that band.

items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: Gerald Wilson was making arrangements for us, Dudley Brooks, and Billy Strayhorn.

ctx.x: So they wouldn't allow Lester to play with the band when he first arrived, and they told him that he had to appear as a guest; he could play three sets a night --but he had to play on the floor, he couldn't play on the bandstand with the band. And so he would come to Billy Berg's, and he had a little; he would set out back all night on a milk box waiting to come on, and we would play a set; we would play 3 sets a night, and then we would introduce Lester Young, and he'd come out and stand in the middle of the…

Well, then, they made him do this for 6 weeks, while he put his transfer in, and after that, then he could play with us. We had a very good band, because -- I'll tell you who made the arrangements for us -- Gerald Wilson was making arrangements for us, Dudley Brooks, and Billy Strayhorn.
